title: Brahman, born first in the east

words.role: subject (or object) of the first line
words.context: Sāyaṇa: the gold plate as Brahman, «रुक्मस्वरूपं ब्रह्म»

words.meaning: from the boundary, from the horizon
belonging to the depths, of the base
words.context: Sāyaṇa: things of the earth, the base

words.gram: pres. participle of √अस्, n. gen. sg.

words.role: main verb of the second line

morphology.note: vi + the aorist of √vṛ, ‘uncovered’, with the augment and ending contracted (vi-avar).

translation.literal: Brahman, born first in the east, the Vena uncovered from the boundary, the bright ones; he [uncovered] the deep likenesses, the stations of this, he uncovered the womb of the existent and of the non-existent.
translation.readable: Brahman was born first, in the east; the Bright One opened the shining rays from the horizon. He laid bare the deep forms of this world and their places — he uncovered the womb of what is and of what is not.

meaning: A verse of creation and revelation (TS 4.2.8.2). Brahman is born first, in the east; Vena, ‘the longing one’, whom Sāyaṇa takes as the lovely sun, opens the bright rays from the horizon and uncovers the deep forms of the world and the womb of both the existent and the non-existent. In the Saṃhitā it accompanies the placing of the rukma, a gold plate, on a lotus leaf at the centre of the fire altar: Sāyaṇa reads the gold plate as Brahman and the rising sun as its likeness. The verse addresses Brahman, the sacred power.
in_the_rite: The third mantra of Bṛhaspati’s step in the Navagraha sūktam (witness S). S names the adhidevatā and pratyadhidevatā together, so the edition does not say which this verse is for; the verse itself speaks of Brahman. Its use for a graha belongs to the later gṛhya tradition.

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Sāyaṇa quotes the Kalpa for its use in building the fire altar: «पुष्करपर्ण उपरिष्टान्निर्बाधं रुक्ममुपधाय» — the gold plate, studded with knobs, is laid on the lotus leaf.

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Sāyaṇa: «प्रथमं जज्ञानमादावुत्पन्नमिदं रुक्मस्वरूपं ब्रह्म» — the gold plate is Brahman, born first; the sun is its likeness, Vena being «कमनीयः सूर्यः», the lovely sun, who opened his rays in the east.

notes.label: linguistic
notes.text: A triṣṭubh; the same verse opens the Vena hymn of the Atharvaveda (4.1.1), which is not among this edition’s sources and is not quoted here.
